concepts.name: Origins and Evolution of BRICS: From Acronym to Institution
key_dimensions: Jim O'Neill's 2001 Goldman Sachs coinage of 'BRIC' vs. its transformation into a formal geopolitical grouping
First formal BRIC Summit (Yekaterinburg, 2009) vs. first BRICS Summit after South Africa's inclusion (Sanya, 2011)
Distinction between BRIC as an economic concept and BRICS as a political-diplomatic forum
UPSC trap: South Africa joined in 2010 (invited) but first attended as full member at 2011 Sanya Summit — year confusion is common

concepts.name: BRICS Membership Criteria and Expansion Logic
key_dimensions: Original selection rationale: large population, landmass, GDP growth potential, and regional influence
Absence of formal membership criteria document — contrast with WTO/IMF accession protocols
2023 Johannesburg Summit expansion: invitation to Argentina, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE (Argentina later declined under Milei)
UPSC trap: distinguishing 'invited' vs. 'full members' vs. 'partner states' — new 'BRICS Partner Country' category introduced 2024

concepts.name: BRICS Summits: Hosting Pattern, Key Declarations, and Thematic Priorities
key_dimensions: Rotation of presidency and hosting rights among members (alphabetical/agreed order)
Key declarations: Fortaleza Declaration (2014 — NDB establishment), Johannesburg Declaration (2023 — expansion)
Thematic shifts: economic cooperation (early years) → de-dollarisation and reform of multilateral institutions (recent years)
India's BRICS Chairmanship 2021 (virtual): focus on intra-BRICS trade and counter-terrorism

concepts.name: New Development Bank (NDB): Structure, Mandate, and Comparison with Bretton Woods Institutions
key_dimensions: Established by Fortaleza Declaration 2014; headquartered in Shanghai; began operations 2016
Initial authorized capital: $100 billion; equal shareholding (20% each) among founding BRICS members — key UPSC distinction from IMF/World Bank voting structure
Mandate: infrastructure and sustainable development financing in emerging and developing economies
Contrast with World Bank: no conditionalities, no single-country veto, open to non-BRICS membership (Bangladesh, UAE, Egypt, Uruguay admitted) — UPSC trap on membership exclusivity

concepts.name: Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA): Design, Trigger Mechanism, and IMF Linkage
key_dimensions: Established 2014 (Fortaleza); treaty-based framework providing liquidity support during balance-of-payments crises
Total committed size: $100 billion; China contributes $41B, Brazil/Russia/India $18B each, South Africa $5B — unequal contributions unlike NDB
UPSC trap: CRA is NOT a fund (no pooled money) — it is a swap/commitment arrangement, unlike IMF's actual lending pool
IMF linkage trap: beyond 30% of a country's quota, CRA disbursement is conditional on an IMF programme — making it partially dependent on Bretton Woods architecture it seeks to rival

concepts.name: BRICS and De-dollarisation: Rhetoric vs. Reality
key_dimensions: Push for trade settlement in local currencies and reducing USD dependence in intra-BRICS trade
Proposals for a common BRICS currency — discussed at 2023 Johannesburg Summit but not adopted; no formal roadmap exists
UPSC trap: No BRICS currency has been created; confusing discussion/proposals with actual decisions is a common error
Structural constraints: capital account convertibility differences, exchange rate volatility, absence of a central monetary authority among members

concepts.name: BRICS vs. G20: Overlaps, Distinctions, and Strategic Complementarity
key_dimensions: All BRICS members are G20 members, but G20 includes advanced economies (US, EU, Japan) — BRICS is exclusively emerging/developing
G20 has formal Secretariat rotation; BRICS has no permanent secretariat — coordination through Sherpas and working groups
BRICS uses G20 as a platform to coordinate positions (e.g., IMF quota reform, WTO dispute settlement reform)
UPSC trap: BRICS is not a subset of G20 institutionally — they are parallel forums with overlapping membership

concepts.name: BRICS Economic Weight: GDP, Trade, and Population Share — Data and Interpretation
key_dimensions: Combined BRICS (original 5) GDP at PPP surpassed G7 around 2020 — significance and caveats of PPP vs. nominal GDP comparison
Share of global trade (~17-18% intra and extra combined) vs. G7's dominance in financial flows
UPSC trap: BRICS economies are not uniformly 'emerging' — Russia and South Africa have had stagnation; conflating growth potential with current performance
Post-expansion BRICS+ share in global oil production (Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Russia) — energy geopolitics angle

concepts.name: BRICS Institutional Architecture: Working Groups, Forums, and People-to-People Pillars
key_dimensions: Three pillars: Political-Security (Track I), Economic-Financial (Track II), Cultural-People-to-People (Track III)
Key Track II bodies: BRICS Business Council, BRICS Women's Business Alliance, BRICS Interbank Cooperation Mechanism
BRICS Academic Forum and Young Diplomats Forum — soft power and Track 1.5 diplomacy
Absence of a permanent secretariat: UPSC trap — often confused with SCO or ASEAN which have permanent secretariats

concepts.name: India's Strategic Interests in BRICS
key_dimensions: Platform for multipolarity advocacy and reform of UNSC, IMF, and WTO
NDB as alternative infrastructure financing without Western conditionalities
Tension: India-China bilateral disputes (Galwan, border tensions) vs. continued BRICS engagement — UPSC tests this contradiction
India's use of BRICS to push counter-terrorism norms (listing of Pakistan-based terrorists) — often blocked by China, revealing limits of consensus

concepts.name: BRICS and Reform of Multilateral Institutions
key_dimensions: Consistent demand for IMF quota reform to reflect emerging economy weight (currently underrepresented)
Push for developing-country representation in World Bank leadership — challenging the informal US-Europe convention on WB/IMF heads
WTO reform: support for restoring Appellate Body functionality; opposition to developed-country agricultural subsidies
UPSC trap: BRICS seeks reform of multilateral institutions, not their replacement — nuance often tested

concepts.name: BRICS Expansion 2023–2024: New Members, Partner Countries, and Geopolitical Implications
key_dimensions: Full members from Jan 2024: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE (Argentina declined) — 5 new members, not 6
New 'BRICS Partner Country' category (2024, Russia's presidency): 13 countries including Algeria, Cuba, Indonesia, Nigeria, Turkey, Vietnam — distinct from full membership
Geopolitical signal: inclusion of Iran (under US sanctions) and Saudi Arabia (US ally) simultaneously — tests non-alignment and consensus limits
UPSC trap: distinguishing 'full members,' 'invited members who declined,' and 'partner countries' — three distinct categories post-2023

concepts.name: BRICS Counter-Terrorism and Security Cooperation Framework
key_dimensions: BRICS Counter-Terrorism Strategy adopted at 2020 Moscow Summit — first formal CT document
BRICS Counter-Terrorism Working Group (CTWG) and its five sub-working groups (financing, travel, internet, etc.)
India's push to name Pakistan-based groups (LeT, JeM) in BRICS declarations — Chinese resistance and diplomatic bargaining
UPSC trap: BRICS has a security/CT dimension that is frequently overlooked — it is not purely an economic grouping

concepts.name: NDB vs. Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB): Comparison and Overlap
key_dimensions: NDB: BRICS-founded, equal voting, Shanghai HQ, infrastructure + sustainable development focus
AIIB: China-led, weighted voting (China ~26%), Beijing HQ, broader Asian membership including European countries
Key distinction: NDB has equal founder shareholding; AIIB has China as dominant shareholder — UPSC frequently tests this
Both are non-Bretton Woods MDBs but AIIB has more members (~106) vs. NDB's selective expansion; India is a founding member of both

concepts.name: BRICS Energy Cooperation and Resource Geopolitics
key_dimensions: Post-2023 expansion: BRICS+ controls ~42% of global oil production (Russia, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Iran, Brazil)
BRICS Energy Research Cooperation Platform and discussions on energy security
Tension between BRICS fossil fuel exporters and climate commitments of other members (India, South Africa's coal dependence)
UPSC angle: BRICS expansion is partly an energy geopolitics move — overlap with OPEC+ membership of Saudi Arabia, UAE, Russia

concepts.name: BRICS Digital Economy and Technology Cooperation Agenda
key_dimensions: BRICS Digital Economy Partnership Framework and working groups on AI, cybersecurity, and digital trade
Competing digital ecosystems: China's push for data sovereignty norms vs. India and Brazil's different regulatory approaches
BRICS Remote Sensing Satellite Constellation — data-sharing arrangement for earth observation, disaster management, agriculture
UPSC trap: BRICS has a space/satellite cooperation dimension (Remote Sensing Constellation) often overlooked in standard material

concepts.name: BRICS Health Cooperation: Vaccine Equity and Pandemic Response
key_dimensions: BRICS Vaccine R&D Centre network and joint vaccine development framework
COVID-19 context: BRICS nations as major vaccine producers (India — Covishield/Covaxin, Russia — Sputnik V, China — Sinovac/Sinopharm)
BRICS Traditional Medicine cooperation — soft diplomacy angle, India's Ayurveda promotion within framework
Contrast with COVAX: BRICS bilateral vaccine diplomacy vs. multilateral COVAX mechanism — UPSC may test India's dual engagement

concepts.name: Internal Contradictions and Structural Weaknesses of BRICS
key_dimensions: India-China strategic rivalry coexisting within the same forum — tests viability of consensus-based decision-making
Absence of a free trade agreement among BRICS members — unlike ASEAN or EU, no preferential trade arrangement
Divergent political systems (democracy vs. authoritarian) and economic models creating value alignment challenges
UPSC trap: BRICS is often projected as a unified bloc but decisions require consensus, making collective action on contentious issues (terrorism listing, currency) very difficult

concepts.name: BRICS Financial Inclusion and Sustainable Development Agenda
key_dimensions: NDB's focus on Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and green infrastructure — alignment with Paris Agreement
BRICS Rapid Information Security Channel and financial information exchange mechanisms
BRICS Framework for Responsible Artificial Intelligence — 2023 addition to cooperation agenda
UPSC angle: NDB's lending record includes COVID emergency loans and green bonds — testing whether candidates know NDB's actual portfolio beyond infrastructure
